faq_heading: New construction in University, Vancouver: your questions answered

faq.q: What have condos in University, Vancouver sold for?
faq.a: 153 condos sold in University, Vancouver at a median of $925,000, with the middle half between $795,800 and $1,137,000.

faq.q: How long do homes take to sell in University, Vancouver?
faq.a: In University, Vancouver, townhomes were quickest at 10 days at a median, and houses slowest at 61 days.

faq.q: Which homes in University, Vancouver are the newest?
faq.a: Of the homes that resold in University, Vancouver, condos had the newest median build year, 2015.

items.t: University, Vancouver: 12 houses sold at a median of $1,549,000, with the middle half between $1,280,000 and $4,018,525. The median house took 61 days to sell and closed at 95.0% of list.

29 townhomes sold in University, Vancouver at a median of $1,365,000 (middle half $1,178,000 to $1,988,000). A typical townhome in University, Vancouver spent 10 days on the market and closed at 96.0% of the asking price.
In University, Vancouver, condos sold at a median of $925,000 across 153 sales, and the middle half closed between $795,800 and $1,137,000. The median condo sat 29 days and sold for 96.4% of list.

blocks.text: Source: Paragon closed sales, November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026; medians need 5 or more sales.
How University compares with the rest of Vancouver West

items.t: Houses in University have the lowest median of the 17 Vancouver West sub-areas, $1,549,000, below Marpole at $1,800,000; the highest is Shaughnessy at $4,817,500.

Townhomes in University have the 12th highest median of 18 Vancouver West sub-areas, $1,365,000. False Creek is lowest at $850,000 and Coal Harbour highest at $2,255,000. Marpole ($1,198,000) sits just below and Kitsilano ($1,405,000) sits just above.

Of 21 Vancouver West sub-areas with 5 or more condo sales, University ranks 6th highest at $925,000; the range is $613,500 (Marpole) to $1,228,000 (Coal Harbour). Shaughnessy ($922,500) sits just below and Quilchena ($930,000) sits just above.

blocks.text: By build year, condos are the newest homes selling in University, Vancouver (median 2015) and houses the oldest (median 1972), a gap of 43 years.
